newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria sees 1997 tobacco output sharply higher.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria sees 1997 tobacco output sharply higher.

text.p: Bulgaria's agriculture ministry is forecasting 1997 tobacco output of 71,000 tonnes, compared to 39,790 tonnes in 1996 and to a record low output of 25,000 tonnes in 1995.
A ministry plan set the tobacco area at 48,100 hectares, up from last year's 27,863.
Todor Staikov, senior official from a private tobacco company, said the targets would be reached only if state-owned tobacco factories paid private growers in advance.
"The ministry's figures could be reached only if tobacco factories get funds to pay in advance to tobacco growers and if the minimum purchasing prices are favourable," he said.
He said unfavourable weather conditions and low purchase prices had hindered the sector last year.

"The (minimum purchasing) prices set by the cabinet were low, given the country's higher inflation and its general severe economic situation," he said. "This is why providing incentives (to private tobacco growers) will be crucial."
Under a cabinet decision from last year producers also qualify for additional payments from the state Tobacco Fund.
Tobacco growing is a traditional industry in Bulgaria where it provides a livelihood for some 800,000 people or nearly 10 percent of the country's population, mainly of Turkish origin.

Seven years ago, when tobacco output reached some 100,000 to 150,000 tonnes annually, the Balkan country exported some 40,000 tonnes of tobacco to the former Soviet Union and only some 10,000 to western buyers.
Since the collapse of Eastern Bloc trade links Bulgaria's tobacco exports have started going mainly to western companies.
